newsitem.title: CANADA: Xillix in talks for new LIFE partnerships.
newsitem.headline: Xillix in talks for new LIFE partnerships.

text.p: Xillix Technologies Corp said Tuesday it is talking with potential partners to develop and distribute new applications for its LIFE cancer imaging and detection system.
Xillix President Pierre LeDuc told Reuters after the company's annual meeting that the talks are focused on LIFE devices for use in the bladder, larynx, pharynx, cervix and ovaries.
"We are talking to people now," he said. The negotiations are likely to take six to eight months, he said.
He declined to identify the companies involved but said they were worldwide leaders on par with Olympus Optical Co Ltd of Japan, Xillix's partner on two applications.

Xillix signed an agreement earlier this year with Olympus to distribute its LIFE-Lung fluorescence endoscopy system for lung cancer detection. Xillix and Olympus are also jointly developing a LIFE system for gastrointestinal tract cancers.
The LIFE systems use laser light to activate natural fluorescence in tissue. This allows doctors to detect subtle abnormalities and cancers more easily than with traditional white-light scopes.

Trials of the lung cancer system have found a 171 percent improvement in detection of cancerous and precancerous lesions. Xillix estimates the worldwide market for its lung and gastrointestinal devices at US$3.75 billion.
LIFE-Lung received U.S. regulatory approval last September.
The company aims to begin clinical trials of the gastrointestinal system this year and obtain Japanese and European approvals for the lung system, LeDuc said.
While Xillix may record some profitable quarters, it does not expect to achieve commercial profitability for about three years, he said.
